questions.q: According to the nitrogen rule, a compound with an odd-numbered molecular-ion m/z contains:
c: An odd number of nitrogen atoms
An even number of nitrogen atoms
questions.e: For molecules made of C, H, O, N, halogens, S, P, the nominal molecular weight is odd when N count is odd.

questions.q: M and M+2 peaks of roughly equal intensity (1:1) indicate:
The McLafferty rearrangement of 2-pentanone gives a prominent fragment at m/z:
questions.e: γ-Hydrogen transfer to the carbonyl oxygen and β-cleavage lose propene (42) from M = 86 to give 58.

questions.q: The base peak in the EI mass spectrum of 2-butanone (M = 72) is:
questions.e: α-Cleavage on the ethyl side gives CH₃CO⁺ at 43.

questions.q: The C=O stretch of a saturated aliphatic ketone appears near:
questions.e: About 1715 cm⁻¹; conjugation lowers it by roughly 30 cm⁻¹.

questions.q: A very broad IR absorption from about 2500 to 3300 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of:
questions.e: Strong hydrogen-bonded dimers give an extremely broad band overlapping C–H stretches.

questions.q: A sharp, medium band near 2250 cm⁻¹ suggests:
Which carbonyl compound has the highest C=O stretching frequency?
questions.e: Electronegative substituents raise the frequency; resonance donation (amide) lowers it.

questions.q: How many distinct ¹H NMR signals does ethyl acetate show?
An ethyl group attached to an electronegative atom typically appears as:
questions.e: n+1 rule: CH₂ sees 3 H, CH₃ sees 2 H.

questions.q: An aldehyde proton usually appears at δ:
questions.e: Strong deshielding by C=O anisotropy. Carboxylic acid OH appears 10–13.

questions.q: An isopropyl group (CH(CH₃)₂) attached to a non-chiral center appears as:
questions.e: The CH sees six equivalent neighbors (septet); the methyls see one H (doublet).

questions.q: A para-disubstituted benzene with two different substituents typically shows in the aromatic region:
questions.e: Two sets of two equivalent protons, each coupling to its ortho neighbor.

The ¹³C NMR chemical shift range for a carbonyl carbon (ketone or aldehyde) is about:
How many ¹³C signals does p-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene) show?
questions.e: CH₃ carbons, ring carbons bearing CH₃, and aromatic CH carbons.

questions.q: In a DEPT-135 spectrum:
c: CH and CH₃ are positive, CH₂ negative, quaternary C absent
CH₂ positive, CH and CH₃ negative

questions.q: The degrees of unsaturation (DBE) of C₆H₇N is:
A compound C₄H₈O shows IR ~1715 cm⁻¹ and ¹H NMR δ 1.05 (t, 3H), 2.14 (s, 3H), 2.47 (q, 2H). Identify it and justify.
questions.m: 2-Butanone (CH₃COCH₂CH₃). DBE = 1 (C=O at 1715 cm⁻¹, ketone). The ethyl group gives the t/q pair (1.05/2.47, the CH₂ deshielded by the carbonyl) and the singlet at 2.14 is the methyl ketone CH₃.

questions.q: A compound C₉H₁₀O shows IR 1685 cm⁻¹ and ¹H NMR δ 1.2 (t, 3H), 2.95 (q, 2H), 7.4–7.9 (m, 5H). Identify it.
questions.m: Propiophenone (1-phenylpropan-1-one, PhCOCH₂CH₃). DBE = 5 (benzene ring 4 + C=O 1). C=O at 1685 cm⁻¹ is lowered by conjugation with the aryl ring; the ethyl group appears as t/q with the CH₂ deshielded by the carbonyl; the 5H multiplet is a monosubstituted phenyl ring.
